- Chamelaucium is a genus of shrubs endemic to south western Western Australia.
- Chamelaucium is also known as waxflower.
- Chamelaucium belongs to the myrtle family Myrtaceae.
- Chamelaucium has flowers similar to those of tea-trees in the genus Leptospermum.
- Vanilla is a flavoring derived from orchids of the genus Vanilla.
- Vanilla is derived primarily from the Mexican species flat-leaved vanilla, V. planifolia.
- Verticordia habrantha has hairy sepals that are mostly hidden by round, unfringed petals.
- Verticordia habrantha resembles shrubs in the genus Chamelaucium and is closely related to Chamelaucium.
